rows.jp: 蝉がうるさい。
rows.en: The cicadas were deafening.

ghs.en: The cicadas are making loud,
ghs.assessment: The source simply says the cicadas are loud or noisy; 'making loud' is incomplete English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The cicadas are loud' or 'The cicadas are making a racket.'

rows.jp: こんな暑いのに。
rows.en: Even in heat like this.

ghs.en: even when it's this hot.

rows.jp: 奴らはいつだって本気だ。
rows.en: Those bastards were always all in.

ghs.en: Those guys are always serious.

rows.jp: 「しかし」
rows.en: “Still...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well then."
ghs.assessment: The conjunction marks contrast or reservation, whereas 'well then' advances to a conclusion or next action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Still,' 'But,' or another contrastive discourse marker.

rows.jp: どうするかな、これから。
rows.en: What was I going to do now?

ghs.en: What do I do now.

rows.jp: 屋上が炎天下となると、涼める場所はさほどない。
rows.en: With the rooftop baking under the sun, my options for somewhere cool were limited.

ghs.en: With the rooftop under the blazing sun, that's not really a place to cool off in.
ghs.assessment: The source says that with the rooftop exposed to the blazing sun there are few places available to cool off; the rendering merely excludes the roof itself and omits the scarcity of alternatives.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the conclusion that few cooling-off places remain.

highlights.text: that's not really a place to cool off in

rows.jp: 手近な教室をのぞいてみると、案の定授業中だった。
rows.en: I peeked into the nearest classroom. As expected, class was in session.

ghs.en: I tried peeking inside a class nearby, sure enough, a lesson was in progress.
ghs.assessment: The two independent clauses are joined only by a comma; the source relation is clear but the English sentence is mechanically defective.
ghs.remedy: Separate the clauses or join them with a conjunction or dash.

rows.jp: 一年Ｅ組。
rows.en: First-year Class E.

ghs.en: First Year, Class E.

rows.jp: まちこ先生が授業をしている。
rows.en: Machiko was teaching.

ghs.en: The class is being taught by Machiko-sensei.

rows.jp: 佐藤真智子。
rows.en: Machiko Satō.

ghs.en: Satou Machiko.

rows.jp: 身長１７３センチの長身でグラマラスなダイナマイト・ボディの持ち主でしかも美形でパリッとしていてブランドものの縁なし眼鏡が似合っていて濃紺の光沢を持ったロングヘアを――
rows.en: At 173 centimeters she was tall, glamorous, and built like a bombshell; strikingly beautiful, always impeccably dressed, with designer rimless glasses that suited her and long hair gleaming deep navy—

ghs.en:
Beguiling not just by being the possessor of
a Glamorous Dynamite Body of the impressive
height of 173cm that is nevertheless
beautifully shaped as well as being posh with
those brand-name rimless glasses that so suit her
and her long hair with its dark blue highlights
that in ample fashion-consciousness she keeps in
a tied-up hairdo but by having bewitching
glossied fleshy lips as well, she ranks among the
strongest life-forms in my tastes.

rows.jp: しゃれっ気たっぷりにアップにしているばかりか艶めかしくつやめく肉厚の唇が魅惑的な、俺的最強生命体の一人である。
rows.en: —worn up with effortless style, and full, glossy lips so sensuous they made her one of the most powerful life-forms in my personal taxonomy.

rows.jp: 教職二年目。
rows.en: This was her second year teaching.

ghs.en: In her second year of teaching profession.
ghs.assessment: The fragment means that this is her second year as a teacher; the English omits the article and uses an unnatural construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her second year as a teacher.'

rows.jp: 俺たちと同じ年度で教師になった。
rows.en: She had joined the faculty the same year we entered the school.

ghs.en:
She had became teacher for the same class
year as us.
ghs.assessment: The source says she became a teacher in the same academic year that the students began; it does not say she became a teacher for their class year, and the verb form is also wrong.
ghs.remedy: State the parallel timing of her starting as a teacher and their school year.

highlights.text:
became teacher for the same class
year as us

rows.jp: 今ではすっかり女教師が板についている。
rows.en: By now, she looked every inch the schoolteacher.

ghs.en:
Nowadays female teachers are something
pretty habitual,
ghs.assessment: The idiom says she has now thoroughly settled into or grown into the role of female teacher; the rendering generalizes to female teachers as a habitual phenomenon.
ghs.remedy: Keep her as the subject and render the idiom as being fully at home in the role.

highlights.text:
female teachers are something
pretty habitual

rows.jp: だがまちこ先生は罪深い。
rows.en: But Machiko was a sinful woman.

ghs.en: nevertheless, Machiko-sensei is sinful.

rows.jp: 罪っ子である。
rows.en: A regular Sinderella.

ghs.en: Sinful to the core.
ghs.assessment: The source coins a playful child-or-girl label from 'sin'; the rendering replaces that wordplay with an unsupported intensifier.
ghs.remedy: Recreate a compact playful label rather than escalating degree.

rows.jp: その罪の多くは、シャツを内側から突き上げるふくらみに含まれていると言ってもいいだろう。
rows.en: And a great many of her sins resided in the curves straining upward against her blouse.

ghs.en:
It could probably be said that this wealth of
sins does include protrusions that force upwards
her shirt from the inside.
ghs.assessment: The image of the swelling that pushes up her shirt from within is recognizable, but the verb placement and plural abstraction are unidiomatic and obscure the mock claim that much of her sin resides there.
ghs.remedy: Make the swelling the clear object in which the sins reside and use natural English word order.

highlights.text:
does include protrusions that force upwards
her shirt

rows.jp: ボディ自体はすらりと細長いのに胸の量感はたっぷりで今にも破れるんじゃないか破れた瞬間のπモーションは何万ポリゴンで左右別々に違う動きを見せてさぞかし壮観であるに違いない――
rows.en: The rest of her was long and slender, but her breasts strained against the fabric as if it might burst at any moment. And when it did, the spectacle would surely be breast-in-class physics—tens of thousands of polygons, the left and right moving independently—

ghs.en:
The body itself may be slender and well-
proportioned yet the breasts are abundantly
voluminous so that at any moment they would
tear the shirt wouldn't they and the PI-shaped
motions at the instant of tearing would make
display of thousands and thousands of polygons
in separate independent left-right motions a
most definitely magnificent view no mistake,
and I became so immersed in this kind of thoughts
when I was taking her bewitching classes that I
became fairly worthless from a multiplicity of
angles.

rows.jp: という思考にどっぷり浸かってしまうほどに蠱惑的な彼女の授業を、受けている時の俺は多角的にかなりダメになる。
rows.en: Her lessons were so intoxicating that whenever I attended one, I became a failure of a human being from several different angles at once.

rows.jp: 臀部はと言えばこれまた凶悪で、凶器となっている。
rows.en: Her ass was every bit as vicious: an ass-ault weapon.

ghs.en:
And speaking of her buttocks, their sheer
infernal diabolicalness would make them
a dangerous weapon by themselves,

rows.jp: キレた１４歳の少年が手にするナイフと同じほどに危険だ。
rows.en: As dangerous as a knife in the hand of an enraged fourteen-year-old.

ghs.en:
equally as dangerous as a knife in the
hands of a broken 14-year old boy.
ghs.assessment: The adjective describes a fourteen-year-old who has snapped or flown into a rage, not a boy who is broken.
ghs.remedy: Use an idiomatic phrase for an enraged or unhinged fourteen-year-old.

rows.jp: タイトスカートの内側という男子垂涎の空間に押し込められ、
rows.en: Crammed into the boy-maddening confines of a tight skirt, it seemed to protest:

rows.jp: 『こんな狭い場所じゃあちきの美肉はリラックスできないわよ！』
rows.en: ‘My luscious meat can’t relax in a cramped little joint like this!’

rows.jp: と言わんばかりに張りつめるまろやかヒップ。
rows.en: So spoke the smooth, magnificently taut rump.

ghs.en:
Those round hips under the strain of having been
crammed tight into the Area of Youthful Male
Covetousness known as the depths of her Tight
Skirt seemed to say,

rows.jp: 尻の割れ目に横筋が橋を張るほどにぱっつんぱっつんなスカートの中央に、カッターで縦の切れ目をスーッと入れたいと思ったことは五度や十度じゃない。
rows.en: The skirt pulled so tight that a horizontal crease bridged the cleft beneath it. More than five times—more than ten—I had wanted to run a box cutter straight down the center and set it free.

ghs.en:
With a stritch and a stretch the cleft of the
ass created transversal stripes stretched like
bridges in the middle of her skirt that I thought
not five nor ten times to get a cutter and
caaarefully cut them transversally.
ghs.assessment: The source imagines making one vertical slit down the center of the tight skirt; the rendering changes both the direction and object to cutting plural stripes transversely.
ghs.remedy: Keep the horizontal bridging lines as description and the desired cut as a vertical slit in the skirt.

rows.jp: 危険な女性だ。
rows.en: A dangerous woman indeed.

ghs.en: She's a dangerous female.
ghs.assessment: The source calls her a dangerous woman; the nominal use of 'female' is needlessly clinical and unnatural in this narration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'dangerous woman.'

rows.jp: 悪の校長と番長らによって、妹（同校在籍の女生徒……明るく成績優秀でスポーツ万能で男女わけへだてなく人気があったりする）の弱みをネタに脅迫され性悦の極みに堕ちていきかねない。
rows.en: An evil principal and a gang of delinquents could use some vulnerability of her younger sister's—a bright, athletic honor student at the same school, universally adored by boys and girls alike—to blackmail her and send her spiraling into the furthest depths of carnal ecstasy.

ghs.en:
Because of a wicked headmaster and his gang of
ne'er-do-wells, her little sister (female student
enrolled in the same school... brilliant academic
results, excellent at sports and popular with
both genders without distinction) became her
weak point, so that this threatened sibling
may well be what casts her down into the extremes
of forced sexual ecstasy.
ghs.assessment: The woman is blackmailed by villains who exploit leverage involving her younger sister and may thereby be driven into sexual degradation; the rendering makes the threatened sister the agent that casts her down.
ghs.remedy: Keep the villains as agents of the blackmail and the sister as the leverage used against the woman.

highlights.text:
this threatened sibling
may well be what casts her down

rows.jp: そんな仏国書院的な危機から、俺はいつでも彼女を守りたいのである。
rows.en: I was always ready to save her from any crisis straight out of a France Shoin school fantasy.

ghs.en:
I desire to protect her from that danger worthy
of a certain French publishing house forever and
always.

rows.jp: 一年生の時、副担任になったまちこ先生に飽くなきセクハラを繰り返し、ついには授業中に泣かせてしまったうえ三日間無断欠勤をさせてしまったことが、未だに悔やまれる。
rows.en: In my first year, I sexually harassed Machiko—then my assistant homeroom teacher—so relentlessly that I finally made her cry in class and stay home without notice for three days. I still regretted that.

ghs.en:
As a first year student, Machiko-sensei became
our substitute homeroom teacher, and I repeatedly
and insatiably harassed her until eventually I
made her break down in tears in the middle of
class and take a three day leave from work
without permission, an event I still regret.
ghs.assessment: The title is assistant or deputy homeroom teacher, not a substitute temporarily replacing another teacher.
ghs.remedy: Use 'assistant homeroom teacher' or the locally established equivalent.

rows.jp: ……そして俺は停学を食らって、先輩に「停学君」とからかわれるようになった。
rows.en: ...I had been suspended, and Misato had started calling me ‘Suspension Boy.’

ghs.en:
...and then I was struck with suspension, and
Senpai began teasing me as "Suspension-kun".
ghs.assessment: The narrator was suspended or got slapped with a suspension; 'was struck with suspension' is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I got suspended' or an equivalently forceful idiom.

rows.jp: ま、それで親しくなったからいいんだけど。
rows.en: Still, that was how we got close, so it all worked out.

ghs.en: Well, we got closer because of that, so it's good.

rows.jp: さておき。
rows.en: But I digress.

ghs.en: Anyway.

rows.jp: 以来、まちこ先生と俺との接点は消滅した。
rows.en: After that, Machiko and I had no contact at all.

ghs.en:
Ever since, the points of contact between me
and Machiko-sensei have vanished.
ghs.assessment: The source says their opportunities for contact disappeared; the plural technical phrase is a stiff calque that makes the relationship sound geometric.
ghs.remedy: Say that he had no further contact with her.

highlights.text:
points of contact between me
and Machiko-sensei

rows.jp: 二年を待たずして副担が変わり、受け持ち授業からもいなくなった。
rows.en: Before my second year even began, we had a new assistant homeroom teacher, and she no longer taught any of my classes.

ghs.en:
Without waiting for second year the substitute
changed, and she was no more even in the class
she was in charge of.
ghs.assessment: Before his second year, the assistant homeroom assignment changed and she also ceased teaching any of his classes. The rendering again calls her a substitute and does not express whose timetable lost her.
ghs.remedy: State both the changed assistant-homeroom assignment and her disappearance from the narrator's classes.

highlights.text:
the substitute
changed, and she was no more even in the class
she was in charge of

rows.jp: さらば青い思い出。
rows.en: Farewell to the follies of youth.

ghs.en: Fare thee well, memories of the green.
ghs.assessment: The color adjective evokes youth or immaturity here; literal 'memories of the green' is not a functioning English expression.
ghs.remedy: Use 'youthful memories' or recreate the color metaphor idiomatically.

rows.jp: セクハラ、ほどほどにしておけばよかったな。
rows.en: I should’ve kept the harassment within reasonable limits.

ghs.en:
I just wish I had the kept sexual harassment
within moderation.
ghs.assessment: The intended regret about keeping the harassment within bounds is recognizable, but the English contains a basic word-order and article error.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wish I'd kept the sexual harassment within reason.'

rows.jp: でもどうせ嫌われるならもっと揉んでおけばよかった、と考えてる時点で俺はもう終わってるんだろう人として。
rows.en: Then again, if she was going to hate me anyway, I should’ve gotten in a few more squeezes. The fact that this was where my mind went probably meant I was already beyond saving.

ghs.en:
But if being hated was the result no matter what,
then I wish I had given a further once-over to
all that, though having those thoughts at this
point means that I'm all but done as a person.
ghs.assessment: The explicit counter-regret is that he should have groped or fondled more; the vague phrase removes the concrete act that makes his self-condemnation land.
ghs.remedy: Name the groping directly enough to preserve the joke and moral self-indictment.

highlights.text:
given a further once-over to
all that

rows.jp: 「ふー」
rows.en: ‘Whew.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sigh..."

rows.jp: とにかく、このまま廊下をウロウロしてたら誰かに見つかる。
rows.en: In any case, if I kept wandering the halls, someone would find me.

ghs.en: Anyway, if I keep loitering in the corridors like this someone'll find me.

rows.jp: 食券を買ってから部室に行こう。
rows.en: I would buy my lunch ticket and head to the clubroom.

ghs.en: Let's go to the club room after buying a meal ticket.

rows.jp: 完璧計画爆誕。
rows.en: And so the Perfect Plan burst screaming into the world.

ghs.en: The explosive birth of a perfect project.

rows.jp: Ａ定食は三時間目には売り切れるから、確実に食べたい時は一時間目の終わりと同時に食堂に赴くことになる。
rows.en: Set Meal A always sold out by third period. Anyone determined to secure one had to reach the cafeteria the moment first period ended.

ghs.en: Meal set A is usually sold out by third period, so if one wants to eat it with certainty they have to be heading towards the cafeteria as soon as first period is over.

rows.jp: それでも多少、行列はできる。
rows.en: Even then, there was usually a line.

ghs.en: Even then, there's a bit of a line,

rows.jp: 二時間目に遅刻してしまうこともあるわけだ。
rows.en: Enough of one to make you late for second period.

ghs.en: therefore some will come back late for second period at times.

rows.jp: こういうことが多発すると、たまに思い出したように『食券事前買い禁止令』が公布されたりする。
rows.en: Whenever that happened too often, the administration would suddenly remember to promulgate another ‘No Advance Lunch-Ticket Purchases’ decree.

ghs.en: If this happens frequently enough, occasionally they seem to remember to make the official promulgation of the Prohibition of Meal Ticket Pre-Sale.

rows.jp: 数をもっと多く用意してくれればいいのに。
rows.en: They could simply make more meals.

ghs.en: But it'd be better if they just made more of them.

rows.jp: 誰もがそう思う。
rows.en: Everyone thought so.

ghs.en: Everybody thinks that.

rows.jp: だが無駄をはぶくためか、定食は数量限定が鉄の掟。
rows.en: Perhaps to prevent waste, they observed an ironclad rule: only so many set meals.

ghs.en: However, to cut back on waste or something, the set meal being available in limited number is an iron rule.
ghs.assessment: The limited-quantity rule is semantically present, but this count construction is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'available only in limited quantities.'

rows.jp: だからこんな機会を逃す手はない。
rows.en: No way I could pass up a chance like this.

ghs.en: Therefore, there's no way I'm missing this opportunity.

rows.jp: さすがに一限目の途中なら行列もないしな。
rows.en: Halfway through first period, there would not be a soul in line.

ghs.en: As it's midway through first period there shouldn't be a line.

rows.jp: がらすきだった。
rows.en: The place was deserted.

ghs.en: It was almost entirely uninhabited.
ghs.assessment: The place is almost empty or sparsely occupied, not literally without inhabitants or residents.
ghs.remedy: Use 'almost empty.'

rows.jp: 「おばちゃん、エース定食」
rows.en: ‘One Ace Meal, please.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Madam, set meal Ace."
ghs.assessment: The address is a casual call to the cafeteria lady, and the named meal modifies the set-meal noun; the English is overly formal and reverses the name order.
ghs.remedy: Use a casual 'ma'am' or equivalent followed by 'the Ace set meal.'

rows.jp: 無事に食券を買えた。
rows.en: I bought my ticket without incident.

ghs.en: I was able to buy my meal ticket without problems.

rows.jp: らくちんらくちん。
rows.en: Easy-peasy.

ghs.en: Easy life mine, just an easy life.
ghs.assessment: The repeated playful adjective means that the task was easy or easy-peasy; the rendering invents an ungrammatical claim about an easy life.
ghs.remedy: Use a light repeated expression such as 'Easy, easy.'

highlights.text: Easy life mine, just an easy life

rows.jp: 部室に入ると、パイプ椅子に座って雑誌を読んでいた男が顔をあげた。
rows.en: When I entered the clubroom, a boy sitting in a folding chair looked up from his magazine.

ghs.en: On entering the club room, a male who was sitting on a folding chair and reading a magazine raised his head.
ghs.assessment: The source refers to a man; nominal 'a male' is clinical and unnatural for ordinary narrative identification.
ghs.remedy: Use 'a man.'

rows.jp: 「いやいやいや、友貴先生じゃないですか」
rows.en: ‘Well, well, well. If it isn't Professor Tomoki.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well well well, if it isn't Tomoki-sensei."

rows.jp: 「こんなところで奇遇ですな。先生もアレですか？　こっちの方もいける口で？」
rows.en: ‘Fancy meeting you here. Are you also a devotee of... the ladies?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "What a coincidence finding you here. Are you doing 'that' as well, Sensei? You will offer me something to wet my lips as well?"
ghs.assessment: Together with the raised-pinky gesture, the speaker is insinuating that the other man is also interested in that sort of partner or pursuit. The rendering instead asks to be offered a drink, eliminating the insinuation and gesture-dependent joke.
ghs.remedy: Use an indirect but intelligible question that connects the pinky gesture to being interested in women.

highlights.text: You will offer me something to wet my lips as well

rows.jp: 小指を立てる。
rows.en: I raised my pinkie.

ghs.en: I raise a pinky.

rows.en: ‘Uh... sure.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Well..."

rows.jp: 冴えない顔でそう応じる。
rows.en: He answered without enthusiasm.

ghs.en: He answers with a sullen face.
ghs.assessment: The expression is dull, listless, or unenthused; 'sullen' adds resentment or petulance not present in the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'with an unenthusiastic expression' or equivalent.

rows.jp: 友貴は防御時のアドリブが全然きかないタイプだ。
rows.en: Tomoki had no capacity whatsoever for improvising under fire.

ghs.en: Tomoki's the type that just can't ad-lib an effective counter on time.

rows.jp: コンパでは善人だが退屈な男と分類されるに違いない。
rows.en: At a mixer, he would inevitably be filed under nice guy, boring company.

ghs.en: At a social mixer he'd be categorized as the nice but boring guy, no mistake.

rows.jp: 「さぼりか？　さぼりなのか？」
rows.en: ‘Cutting class? Are we cutting class?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Cutting? Cutting aren't you?"
ghs.assessment: The repeated accusation is that he is skipping class. The bare verb 'cutting' does not carry that sense here, and the tag-like repetition is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use an idiomatic repeated accusation such as 'Skipping class? You are, aren't you?'

rows.jp: 「そっちこそ」
rows.en: ‘Look who's talking.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "You too."

rows.jp: 「うちのクラスは自習になったんだ」
rows.en: ‘Our class got a study period.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Our class became self-study, 's all."
ghs.assessment: The class was assigned a self-study period; a class cannot idiomatically 'become self-study.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Our class has a self-study period.'

rows.jp: 再び雑誌に目を戻し、パックのコーヒー牛乳をすすった。
rows.en: He returned to his magazine and sipped coffee milk from a carton.

ghs.en: Returning his eyes to the magazine once again, he sipped coffee milk from a carton.

rows.jp: なるほど。
rows.en: Made sense.

ghs.en: I see.

rows.jp: それで抜け出して、ここでくつろいでるわけだ。
rows.en: So he had slipped out to relax here.

ghs.en: He slipped out of that, then he came here to relax a bit.

rows.jp: いいひと属性のくせしてワルぶりやがって。
rows.en: Playing the bad boy when the nice-guy trait was baked into his character sheet. The nerve.

ghs.en: That damnable vice of people with the Nice Guy Attribute of acting worse than they are.
ghs.assessment: The narrator mocks this particular nice guy for putting on a bad-boy act. The rendering turns it into a generalized vice shared by a category of people and weakens the direct sneer.
ghs.remedy: Keep the individual as subject: despite his nice-guy trait, he is trying to act bad.

highlights.text: vice of people with the Nice Guy Attribute of acting worse than they are

rows.jp: 「食券は？」
rows.en: ‘Lunch ticket?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Meal ticket?"

rows.jp: 「買ったよ」
rows.en: ‘Bought it.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Bought it."

rows.jp: 「やるな」
rows.en: ‘Not bad.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Not bad."
Tomoki: "..."

rows.jp: シカトかい。
rows.en: Ignoring me, huh?

ghs.en: Ostracism?
ghs.assessment: The slang complaint means that he is being ignored or given the silent treatment, not socially ostracized.
ghs.remedy: Use a colloquial complaint such as 'Ignoring me, huh?'

rows.jp: なんか気が抜けた。
rows.en: That took the wind out of my sails.

ghs.en: That sends me down a bit.
ghs.assessment: The narrator feels deflated or has the wind taken out of him; 'sends me down' is vague and non-idiomatic.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That kind of deflated me.'

rows.jp: どだい放送部はキャラ的分業化が進んでいて、ツッコミ担当の友貴に悪ノリは期待できない。
rows.en: The Broadcasting Club had long since achieved complete specialization by character role, and there was no point expecting Tomoki, our designated straight man, to join me in a bit.

ghs.en: The division of characterizational labor in the Broadcast Club is basically voluntary, so it can't be expected for Tomoki to get carried away when he's in charge of the Straight-Man role.
ghs.assessment: The source says the club's division of character roles is already highly developed. It says nothing about the arrangement being voluntary; that invention disrupts the reason a designated straight man cannot be expected to join the escalation.
ghs.remedy: State that the role-based division of labor is firmly established.

rows.jp: 窓から外を見る。
rows.en: I looked out the window.

ghs.en: I looked outside from the window.
ghs.assessment: This immediate narrative action is in the present tense, while the rendering shifts it into the past amid surrounding present-tense narration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I look outside through the window.'

rows.jp: 強い日差し。
rows.en: The sunlight was fierce.

ghs.en: Strong sunshine.

rows.jp: 「暑いな、今日も」
rows.en: ‘Hot again today.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Another hot day today, innit."
ghs.assessment: The source is casual but does not motivate a conspicuously British dialect tag, which imposes an unrelated regional voice.
ghs.remedy: Use a neutral casual tag or omit it.

rows.jp: 「冷蔵庫にもう一個あるけど」
rows.en: ‘There's another one in the fridge.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "There's still one left in the fridge tho."

rows.jp: 「８０円だっけ？」
rows.en: ‘Eighty yen, right?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "80 yen was it?"

rows.jp: 「そー」
rows.en: ‘Right.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Yep."

rows.jp: 「もらうわ」
rows.en: ‘I'll take it.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "I shall be taking it, yes."
ghs.assessment: The source is a casual 'I'll take it'; the rendering imposes conspicuous formality and adds a mannered final affirmation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'll take it.'

highlights.text: I shall be taking it, yes

rows.jp: 突き出た手に小銭を落として、備え付けの冷蔵庫を開ける。
rows.en: I dropped some coins into his outstretched palm and opened the club refrigerator.

ghs.en: I drop coins into the proffered hand, and opened the provisions refrigerator.
ghs.assessment: The coordinated present-tense actions are split across present and past, and the installed or provided refrigerator becomes a nonsensical 'provisions refrigerator.'
ghs.remedy: Keep both verbs in the same tense and describe the built-in or provided refrigerator.

highlights.text: drop coins into the proffered hand, and opened the provisions refrigerator

rows.jp: 「……あの、全部の硬貨に正倉院が刻まれているんですけど？」
rows.en: ‘...Um. Why does every coin have the Shōsōin on it instead of the Phoenix Hall?’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...uhm, but every coin here has the Shoushou-in engraved on it instead of the Byoudou-in...?"

rows.jp: クレームは無視して、パックをすすった。
rows.en: I ignored the complaint and drank from the carton.

ghs.en: Ignoring the objection, I sucked on the carton.
ghs.assessment: He sips the drink from its carton; the rendering makes the carton itself the object being sucked and sounds physically different.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I sipped from the carton.'

rows.jp: 「もう」
rows.en: ‘Come on.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Aww."

rows.jp: それ以上の追求はなく、気怠い時間が流れた。
rows.en: He pursued the matter no further, and the lazy minutes drifted by.

ghs.en: With no further pursuit of the matter, listlessly the time flowed on.
ghs.assessment: The source describes a languid stretch of time passing; the adverb is mechanically attached to time as though time itself behaved listlessly.
ghs.remedy: Use 'a languid silence settled in' or 'time passed languidly.'

rows.jp: 窓際にずらりと並ぶ、様々なモニターと機材を乗せた長テーブルを見やる。
rows.en: I glanced at the long table beneath the windows, crowded with monitors and miscellaneous hardware.

ghs.en: My gaze turns to the several monitors, lined up in a row together with other equipment, arranged on the long table by the window.

rows.jp: 放送部の機材だ。
rows.en: The Broadcasting Club's equipment.

ghs.en: It's the equipment of the Broadcast Club.

rows.jp: すぐ隣が、放送室となっている。
rows.en: The studio itself was next door.

ghs.en: Immediately next door is the Broadcast Room itself.

rows.jp: こっちは待機室で、たまり場だ。
rows.en: This was the greenroom, otherwise known as our den.

ghs.en: This is the ready room, so it's a gathering area.

rows.jp: 電源があるのをいいことに、小型冷蔵庫を置いたりゲーム機を常備したり携帯充電器が一列に並んでいたりと校内でも屈指の無法空間となっている。
rows.en: We had exploited the electrical outlets for all they were worth: a mini-fridge, a permanently installed game console, a whole row of phone chargers. Even by this school's standards, it was a lawless little kingdom.

ghs.en: It's nice that there's electricity, so there's a small refrigerator, game consoles on reserve, and cellphone chargers lined up in a row, making this into the foremost lawless space inside the school.
ghs.assessment: The occupants take advantage of having electrical power as license to install appliances and chargers. The rendering turns that causal criticism into a generic statement that electricity is nice.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Taking full advantage of the power outlets...' or equivalent.

rows.jp: 「あれ、機材の配線外れてない？」
rows.en: ‘Hey, isn't the equipment unplugged?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "My, isn't the wiring of the machine disconnected?"
ghs.assessment: The source refers to the equipment's wiring generally, not the wiring of a single machine.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Isn't the equipment disconnected?' or 'Haven't the cables been unplugged?'

rows.jp: 「新しいマシン組むから、ちょっと構成変える」
rows.en: ‘I'm building a new machine, so I'm changing the setup.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "I'm putting together a new machine, so I'm changing stuff around a bit."

rows.jp: 「ふーん」
rows.en: ‘Huh.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uh-huh."

rows.jp: 友貴はこれでけっこうなパソコン少年で、美希とよくＣＰＵだのメモリだのの会話に花を咲かせている。
rows.en: Tomoki was quite the computer nerd. He and Miki could talk CPUs and memory for hours.

ghs.en: Tomoki here is quite the PC guy, and a lot of conversations bloom between him and Miki about CPU and RAM and those things.

rows.jp: 別の学校に通う一個下の可愛い彼女がいて、出会いはＢＢＳだそうだ。
rows.en: He also had a cute girlfriend one year below us at another school. Apparently they had met on a BBS.

ghs.en: He has a cute girlfriend from another school one year younger than him that he seems to have met on a BBS.

rows.jp: 友貴が入院している頃、一度本人と出会ったことがある。
rows.en: I had met her once while Tomoki was in the hospital.

ghs.en: I once met her myself when Tomoki was hospitalized.

rows.jp: 見舞いに行ったときだ。
rows.en: When I went to visit him.

ghs.en: She came during visiting hours.
ghs.assessment: The narrator met her when he went to visit the hospitalized friend. The rendering reverses the visitor and invents a reference to visiting hours.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was when I went to visit him.'

rows.jp: 『あっ、あの、と、とと友貴くんがお世話になってますっっっ』
rows.en: ‘Oh! Um, T-T-Thank you for looking after Tomoki!’

ghs.en: Girlfriend: 『Ah, uhm, tha-, tha-tha-thank you for taking care of Tomoki-kun...!』

rows.jp: と頭をさげてきた制服の着こなしからして一味違う激キュートな生命体の出現に、ショックを受けた俺の記憶は未だおぼろげだ。
rows.en: The way she wore her uniform already set her apart, and when this ultra-cute life-form bowed to me, the shock hit so hard that my memory of it was still hazy.

ghs.en: And she bowed her head, that Ultra Kyute life form so unique just in the elegant way she wore her uniform, that my memories are still vague from the shock of meeting her.
ghs.assessment: The deliberately misspelled English coinage is unexplained and the surrounding sentence attaches multiple 'that' clauses without a stable structure, blunting the claim that even her uniform styling marked an exceptionally cute life-form.
ghs.remedy: Use a readable comic superlative and rebuild the sentence around the narrator's shock-blurred memory.

rows.jp: 彼女……優花ちゃんは、そのあとも友貴をかいがいしく世話していた。
rows.en: His girlfriend, Yūka, had continued tending to him devotedly afterward.

ghs.en: That girl... Yuka-chan was in the most gallant service of Tomoki even after that.

rows.jp: きっと友貴が求めれば、脱ぎたての下着だってくれるに違いなかった。
rows.en: If Tomoki asked, she would surely hand over the panties she had just taken off.

ghs.en: Make no mistake, if Tomoki were just to ask, she'd strip off and hand over her panties.

rows.jp: 「いてっ！　なにすんの！？」
rows.en: ‘Ow! What was that for?’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "OW-! Whassat for?!"

rows.jp: 「急に悔しくなって……」
rows.en: ‘I got jealous all of a sudden...’

ghs.en: Taichi: "I felt annoyed all of a sudden..."

rows.jp: 「はい、なにが？　わけわかんざき」
rows.en: ‘For what? That makes no sense, Spence.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Huh, with what? I don't get a watch of whatcha sayin'."

rows.jp: 友貴はギャグも最高につまらない。
rows.en: Tomoki's jokes were also catastrophically unfunny.

ghs.en: Even Tomoki's gags are the height of boring.

rows.jp: こんなヤツにあんな可愛いガー（ＧＩＲＬ）がひっつくなんて、間違ってる。不潔。
rows.en: A guy like this landing a cute gurrl like that was just wrong. Obscene.

ghs.en: It's just wrong for that cute GRRR(l) to stick to this guy. It's filthy.
Girl: "...heheh!"
ghs.assessment: The source is a wordless caught-breath or suppressed reaction; explicit laughter is added without support and changes the emotional signal.
ghs.remedy: Use a breath, catch, or nonverbal ellipsis without specifying laughter.

rows.jp: くすくす笑いが聞こえた。
rows.en: I heard a stifled giggle.

ghs.en: I could hear a giggly laugh.

rows.jp: 「あれえ、いたんだ？」
rows.en: ‘Oh, were you there?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Myyy, she was here?"
ghs.assessment: The speaker addresses the newly noticed girl directly: 'Oh, you were here?' The rendering changes the addressee into a third-person subject.
ghs.remedy: Use second person.

rows.jp: 放送室から来たんだろう、眼鏡をかけた小柄な少女がいた。
rows.en: A petite girl in glasses stood nearby, apparently having come from the studio.

ghs.en: A bespectacled girl of small build was there, likely having come out of the broadcast room.

rows.jp: 「あいかわらず先輩がたは……」
rows.en: ‘You two never change...’

ghs.en: Girl: "Always like this, you two Senpai..."

rows.jp: 「がたって」
rows.en: ‘Us two?’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "'You two'..."

rows.jp: 後輩の福原みゆきだった。
rows.en: It was our junior, Miyuki Fukuhara.

ghs.en: She was Fukuhara Miyuki, a Kouhai of mine.

rows.jp: 「おっす。元気？」
rows.en: ‘Hey. You doing okay?’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Hail. In spirits?"
ghs.assessment: The source is an ordinary casual greeting and check-in; the English sounds archaic and omits the grammar needed for a question about wellbeing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hey. How are you?'

rows.jp: 「おやあ？　おやおやぁ？」
rows.en: ‘Oh? Ohoho?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh? Oh-my-myyy?"

rows.jp: 「な、なんです？」
rows.en: ‘W-What is it?’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Wh-, what is it?"

rows.jp: 警戒してのけぞるみゆき。
rows.en: Miyuki leaned away, instantly on guard.

ghs.en: Miyuki leans back guardedly.

rows.jp: 「どーせまた地味だとか言うんですよね？」
rows.en: ‘You're only going to call me plain again, aren't you?’

ghs.en:
Miyuki: "You're still gonna call me plain again are you?"
Taichi: "Why you so plain, why!"
ghs.assessment: The source contains only the narrator's exclamation that she is an extraordinarily plain girl. A full anticipatory response by the girl is invented, and the remaining English line is itself malformed.
ghs.remedy: Remove the invented reply and render the single exclamation idiomatically.

highlights.text: Miyuki: "You're still gonna call me plain again are you?"

rows.jp: 「なんて地味っ娘なんだ」
rows.en: ‘But you are so aggressively plain.’

rows.jp: 「あああああ……」
rows.en: ‘Aaaagh...’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Awwww..."

rows.jp: 少女はがくがくと震えた。
rows.en: The girl began to tremble.

ghs.en: The girl shook with a clattering.
ghs.assessment: The girl trembles violently; 'with a clattering' treats the mimetic manner as an unexplained accompanying object and suggests hard objects striking.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The girl shook violently.'

rows.jp: 「うーん、君はなー、どーしてこう地味なのかなー。どーして君の髪どめのゴムはすごく安そうなの？　どうして眉がこんなにぽわぽわしてるの？　どうしてスカートもっと短くしないの？」
rows.en: ‘Why are you so plain? Why does your hair tie look like it cost three cents? Why are your eyebrows so fluffy? Why won't you shorten that skirt?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yeaaah... whyyy you... whyyy you even so plain! Whyyy does the rubber of your hair bands look so cheap, hm? Why are your eyebrows all thin and faint like this? Why isn't this skirt just a little bit shorter?"
ghs.assessment: The eyebrows are described with a soft, fluffy, or fuzzy mimetic quality, not as thin and faint; the insult's concrete visual target changes.
ghs.remedy: Use an idiomatic description of fluffy or fuzzy eyebrows.

rows.jp: 「きゃあ、スカートはちょっとっ」
rows.en: ‘Eek! Leave my skirt alone!’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Kyah! The skirt, really now..."

rows.jp: 「うーん」
rows.en: ‘Hmm.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yeeeah."

rows.jp: 「首筋を優しく撫でないでくださいよっ、きゃっ、耳に指入れないでぇっ！？」
rows.en: ‘Please stop stroking my neck! Ah! Don't put your finger in my ear!’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Please don't gently stroke the back of my neck! KYAH! Don't put your fingers inside my eaaar!"

rows.jp: 愛撫攻撃。
rows.en: I launched the fondling offensive.

ghs.en: Attack of caresses.

rows.jp: 「もとはいいのにねぇ」
rows.en: ‘You’ve got so much potential, too.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "So the outside is fine theeen!"
ghs.assessment: The phrase says her underlying material or natural looks are good despite her plain styling; it does not contrast an exterior with an interior.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You've got good raw material' or a natural equivalent.

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Huh...?"

rows.jp: 「もったいない、もったいない」
rows.en: ‘What a waste. What a terrible waste.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wasteful, so wasteful!"
ghs.assessment: The exclamation means 'what a waste' repeated, not that the girl is wasteful as an adjective.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What a waste, what a waste.'

rows.jp: 「もったいないから食ーべちゃおっと」
rows.en: ‘Far too good to waste. I think I'll eat you instead.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "So wasteful I wanna eat it aaall!"
ghs.assessment: Because letting her go to waste would be a shame, the speaker playfully decides to eat her up. The rendering uses an impersonal object and adds total consumption rather than directing the tease at the girl.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What a waste—maybe I'll just eat you up.'

rows.en: ‘What?’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Huh?"

rows.jp: かぷりこ
rows.en: Cap'n Crunch.

ghs.en: Caplico!

rows.jp: 身をかがめて、耳にかぶりついたのでした。
rows.en: I bent down and bit her ear.

ghs.en: I bent over her and bit into her ears.
ghs.assessment: The action is biting into one ear; pluralizing it changes the physical image.
ghs.remedy: Use singular 'ear.'

rows.jp: 女の子の香りがしました。
rows.en: She smelled like a girl.

ghs.en: There it was, the smell of young girl.
ghs.assessment: The source says she smelled like a girl. The English omits the needed article or possessive construction and adds a youth qualifier not present in the line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She smelled like a girl' or 'I caught a girl's scent.'

rows.jp: 童話調に言っても、セクハラには違いないが。
rows.en: Telling it like a fairy tale did not make it any less harassment.

ghs.en: I may say this in the tone of a fairy-tale, but make no mistake, this is sexual harassment.

rows.jp: 「あわああああああああっ！！？？」
rows.en: ‘Awaaaaaaaaaah?!’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "AwAaAaAaAaA!!!???"

rows.jp: みゆきがエクスタシーに達した（嘘）。
rows.en: Miyuki attained ecstasy. (She did not.)

ghs.en: Miyuki peaked into ecstasy (lies).
ghs.assessment: The mock narration says she reached ecstasy, followed by a singular admission that this is a lie. 'Peaked into' is not idiomatic and plural 'lies' changes the aside.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miyuki reached ecstasy. (Lie.)'

rows.jp: 「……やめてあげなよ、そこのいじめっ子」
rows.en: ‘...Leave her alone, bully.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...just stop that already, you damn bully."

rows.jp: 「お、なんだなんだ、彼女がいるくせにさらにロックオンか？」
rows.en: ‘What's this? One girlfriend isn't enough, so now you're locking on to another target?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oh, lookie lookie, you got a girlfriend damn you but you're engaging in further Lock-On?"
ghs.assessment: The accusation that he is locking on to another target despite already having a girlfriend is recoverable, but the gerund construction is not grammatical natural dialogue.
ghs.remedy: Use 'you're locking on to someone else too?'

rows.jp: 「か、関係ないだろー！」
rows.en: ‘Th-That has nothing to do with anything!’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Th-, that's got nothing to do with this!"

rows.jp: 「このラブラチオ・スナイパーが」
rows.en: ‘You lovelatio sniper.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why, you Lovellatio Sniper!"

rows.jp: ペッ、と吐き捨てる。
rows.en: I spat the words at him.

ghs.en: Pah!, I spat his way.
ghs.assessment: The narration describes a contemptuous verbal delivery after the interjection; the English instead depicts physical spitting in another person's direction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I spat the words out.'

rows.jp: 「けど俺の恋のライフルは、いつでも地味な君を狙って―――」
rows.en: ‘But the rifle of my love is forever trained on you, Plain Jane—’

ghs.en: Taichi: "But the Rifle of my Love always and forever aimed at plain little---"
ghs.assessment: The intended boast is that his love rifle is always aimed at the plain girl being addressed. The English lacks the finite verb and drops the addressee after an incomplete adjective.
ghs.remedy: Use 'is always aimed at plain little you—'.

highlights.text: always and forever aimed at plain little

rows.jp: 視線を移した瞬間、放送室の扉が閉まった。
rows.en: The instant I turned toward her, the studio door swung shut.

ghs.en: The instant I moved my sight, the Broadcast Room door shut,
ghs.assessment: The source describes shifting one's gaze. 'Moved my sight' is a direct but nonidiomatic lexical transfer.
ghs.remedy: Use 'shifted my gaze.'

rows.jp: 鍵がかかる。
rows.en: The lock clicked.

ghs.en: and the lock turned.

rows.jp: みゆきはもういない。
rows.en: Miyuki had vanished.

ghs.en: Miyuki is no longer among us.
ghs.assessment: The local observation is simply that Miyuki is no longer there. The English idiom conventionally announces death and imports a grave implication absent from the line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miyuki was gone.'

rows.jp: 「ぬう」
rows.en: ‘Ngh.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nmuh."

rows.jp: 素知らぬ顔で漫画を読んでいる友貴を睨む。
rows.en: I glared at Tomoki, who was reading his manga with studied innocence.

ghs.en: I glare at Tomoki, who's reading a manga while pretending nothing happened.

rows.jp: 「その優しさがもてる秘訣ですか？」
rows.en: ‘Is that kindness the secret of your popularity?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is that gentleness perchance the trick to becoming popular?"

rows.jp: 「はあ？」
rows.en: ‘Huh?’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Huh?"

rows.jp: 「まあいいや。それよりみゆきはどうしているの？」
rows.en: ‘Never mind. What’s Miyuki doing in there?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oh, forget it. More importantly, how come Miyuki's here?"

rows.jp: 「……おまえって後輩は平気で呼び捨てるよな」
rows.en: ‘...You never hesitate to call your juniors by name.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...look at you perfectly alright with calling a Kouhai without honorifics."
ghs.assessment: 呼び捨て means addressing someone by name without an honorific or title; it does not specifically require a surname. GHS identifies the omission but leaves kouhai untranslated and renders the observation in strained, unidiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use idiomatic English for casually calling a junior by name without a title.

highlights.text: perfectly alright with calling a Kouhai without honorifics

rows.jp: 「だって後輩だよ？」
rows.en: ‘She's my junior, isn't she?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "She's a Kouhai innshe?"
ghs.assessment: The reply that she is a junior is retained, but the invented eye-dialect contraction is opaque and has no source basis.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She's my junior, isn't she?'

rows.jp: 静寂。
rows.en: Silence.

ghs.en: Silence.

rows.jp: 「そういうとこ尊敬するよ」
rows.en: ‘I admire that about you.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "I respect that part of you."

rows.jp: 「……福原のクラスも自習なんだってさ」
rows.en: ‘...Apparently Fukuhara's class got a study period too.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...Fukuhara's class is also self-study, that's all."
ghs.assessment: The intended information is that Fukuhara's class also has an unsupervised study period. Equating the class itself with 'self-study' is unnatural and imprecise.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Fukuhara's class has study hall too.'

rows.jp: 「あー、なるなる」
rows.en: ‘Ah. Gotcha-gotcha.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, got it, got it."

rows.jp: 謎がとけて興味も失せた。
rows.en: Mystery solved, interest gone.

ghs.en: With the enigma solved the interest vanished.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says that, once the mystery was solved, he also lost interest. The English substitutes a generic definite abstraction and obscures the experiencer.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Once the mystery was solved, I lost interest.'

rows.jp: 「まーた誰か弾けちゃったかな？」
rows.en: ‘Think somebody snapped again?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sooo I just repelled someone again, have I?"
ghs.assessment: The source wonders whether someone has snapped or gone off again. The English makes the speaker an agent who repelled another person, reversing the grammatical and causal structure.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Did somebody snap again, I wonder?'

rows.jp: 「……たぶんな」
rows.en: ‘...Probably.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...mebbe."
ghs.assessment: The nonstandard eye-dialect spelling invents a marked accent not present in the neutral casual Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Probably.'

rows.jp: 椅子に座り直す。
rows.en: I settled back into my chair.

ghs.en: He straightens his sitting posture.
ghs.assessment: The viewpoint narrator reseats himself in the chair. The translation supplies a third-person subject and changes the action into posture correction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I sat back down in the chair.'

rows.jp: 夏の日差しは、まだ室内には入ってこない。
rows.en: The summer sunlight had yet to reach inside the room.

ghs.en: The sunlight of Summer doesn't yet spread throughout the room.
ghs.assessment: The sunlight has not yet entered the room at all; 'doesn't spread throughout' permits partial entry and changes the spatial state.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The summer sunlight hadn't reached the room yet.'

rows.jp: 「放送部はいいよなぁ。この部屋が使えるだけでいい」
rows.en: ‘The Broadcasting Club has it made. Having this room alone is worth joining.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "The Broadcast Club is sooo nice. Nice even just 'cause we can use this room."

rows.jp: 「そうだね」
rows.en: ‘I suppose.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Ain't that right."
ghs.assessment: The source is a low-energy affirmation, 'Yeah' or 'That's true.' The English recasts it as a tag-like demand for agreement and adds marked dialect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Yeah.'

rows.jp: 読書中の友貴は返事も気怠い。
rows.en: Even his replies were listless when he was reading.

ghs.en: Even Tomoki's replies are listless when he's reading.

rows.jp: 「……なに読んでるの？」
rows.en: ‘...What are you reading?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "...what'cha reading there?"

rows.jp: 「サイコマン」
rows.en: ‘Psychoman.’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Psychoman."

rows.jp: 「八束が死んで、真犯人は真崎だと判明した」
rows.en: ‘Yatsuka dies. Masaki was the real killer.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yatsuka dies, the true culprit is proven to be Masaki."
ghs.assessment: The reported revelation is substantially correct, but 'the culprit is proven to be' is an unidiomatic passive construction for a discovery within a narrative.
ghs.remedy: Use 'and Masaki turned out to be the real culprit.'

rows.jp: 「言うなよーっ！！」
rows.en: ‘Don't tell me!’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Don't spoil iiit!!!"

rows.jp: 「やるかーっ！」
rows.en: ‘You want to go?’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wooon't I!"

rows.jp: 「もう言うなよっ、魔獣列島のオチとか絶対言うなよ！」
rows.en: ‘No more spoilers! And don't you dare tell me how Demon-Beast Archipelago ends!’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Don'tcha spoil the rest! And absolutely not the ending of the Islands of the Demons!"

rows.jp: 「アンデルセン神父が味方のスパイでさらわれた依子を助けてくれた！」
rows.en: ‘Father Anderson was their mole, and he rescued Yoriko after she was kidnapped!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Father Anderson rescues the kidnapped Yoriko with help from a friendly spy."
ghs.assessment: The source identifies Father Andersen himself as an allied spy who rescues the abducted person. The English invents a separate friendly spy who assists him.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Father Andersen was an allied spy, and he rescued the kidnapped Yoriko.'

highlights.text: with help from a friendly spy

rows.jp: 「言うなよっ」
rows.en: ‘Stop telling me!’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Don't spoil it!"

rows.jp: 「言論統制反対！」
rows.en: ‘Down with censorship!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Regulation of free speech ostracized!"
ghs.assessment: The line is a slogan opposing censorship or speech control. 'Ostracized' neither expresses opposition nor forms an idiomatic English slogan.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Down with censorship!'

rows.jp: 「裏切りものーっ！」
rows.en: ‘Traitor!’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Traitor!"

rows.jp: 「エピクロス主義者っ！」
rows.en: ‘Epicurean!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Epicurean!"

rows.jp: もみあいに。
rows.en: We grappled.

ghs.en: Push, shove, jostle and struggle.

rows.jp: 中扉が開いて、顔を出したみゆきが小さく叫んだ。
rows.en: The inner door opened, and Miyuki poked her head out with a tiny cry.

ghs.en: The inner door opens, and from Miyuki's peeking face comes a whispered shout.
ghs.assessment: She gives a small or quiet cry after peeking out. 'Whispered shout' is internally contradictory and turns a restrained exclamation into an impossible manner of shouting.
ghs.remedy: Use 'called out softly.'

rows.jp: 「先輩！　先生が来た！」
rows.en: ‘Guys! A teacher's coming!’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Senpai! Teacher's coming!"

rows.jp: 「えっ！」
rows.en: ‘What?!’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Eh?!"

rows.jp: 「あれ……太一？」
rows.en: ‘Wait... Taichi?’

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Wha-... Taichi?"

rows.jp: 馬鹿だな、隠れが遅い。
rows.en: Idiot. Too slow to hide.

ghs.en: Fool, you're slow to hide.

rows.jp: 俺はもう廊下側から死角になる位置に身を潜め終えた。
rows.en: I was already tucked away where no one in the hall could see me.

ghs.en: I was already done concealing myself in a spot blind from the corridor side.
ghs.assessment: The narrator has hidden in a position outside the corridor's line of sight. The English renders the Japanese spatial relation as an unidiomatic 'spot blind from' construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'a spot that couldn't be seen from the corridor.'

highlights.text: a spot blind from the corridor side

rows.jp: 友貴はおたおたと右往左往している。
rows.en: Tomoki darted back and forth in a panic.

ghs.en: Tomoki is flapping about right and left in confusion.
ghs.assessment: The character is panicking and running or looking helplessly this way and that. 'Flapping' suggests wings or loose material and does not idiomatically describe the action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tomoki darted helplessly back and forth.'

rows.jp: 「先輩こっちこっち！」
rows.en: ‘Over here! Hurry!’

ghs.en: Miyuki: "Senpai, here, here!"

rows.jp: 身を低くして、友貴は放送室に逃げた。
rows.en: Keeping low, Tomoki fled into the studio.

ghs.en: Lowering his posture, Tomoki escapes into the Broadcast Room,
ghs.assessment: The source depicts crouching or keeping low while fleeing. 'Lowering his posture' is a literal but nonidiomatic rendering of bodily movement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Keeping low, Tomoki fled into the broadcast room.'

rows.jp: みゆきと一緒に。
rows.en: With Miyuki.

ghs.en: together with Miyuki.

rows.jp: あ、そっちのが良かった……。
rows.en: Oh. I should’ve gone with them...

ghs.en: Ah, I wish I'd done that...

rows.jp: くそ、こんなことくらいで泣くな俺っ。
rows.en: Damn it. Don’t cry over something this stupid, Taichi.

ghs.en: Crap, don't you dare cry over something like this, me!

rows.jp: 扉が締まると同時に、廊下を身長１９０センチの筋肉が通りかかった。
rows.en: The instant the door shut, 190 centimeters of muscle came lumbering down the hall.

ghs.en: Simultaneously with the closing of that door, 190cm of muscle happened to pass by in the corridor.
ghs.assessment: The timing is correct, but the nominalized construction is an unnatural calque where English requires a finite temporal clause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just as the door closed,'

highlights.text: Simultaneously with the closing of that door

rows.jp: マンモスだ。
rows.en: Mammoth.

ghs.en: It's Mammoth.

rows.jp: 萬田重蔵。
rows.en: Jūzō Manda.

rows.jp: 通称マンモス。体罰の天才だ。
rows.en: Known to all as Mammoth. A genius in the art of corporal punishment.

ghs.en: Manda Shigezou.

rows.jp: 見つかったらただではすまない。
rows.en: If he found me, I would not escape intact.

ghs.en: If he finds me, this won't just go away.
ghs.assessment: The source says that being discovered will mean not getting off lightly. The English instead suggests that an abstract situation will persist, losing the threat of consequences to the speaker.
ghs.remedy: Use 'If he catches me, I won't get off easy.'

rows.jp: 以前、奴がスチール缶を片手でピンポン玉ほどのサイズに握りつぶす瞬間を見たことがある。
rows.en: I had once seen him crush a steel can down to the size of a ping-pong ball with one hand.

ghs.en:
Once, I saw this guy instantly crush a steel can
to the size of a ping-pong ball with one hand.

rows.jp: しかもやつの体罰は、21世紀に適応していて侮れない。
rows.en: Worse, his corporal punishment had evolved for the twenty-first century.

ghs.en:
And this guy's corporal punishment is formidably
conforming to the 21st Century.
ghs.assessment: The source says his corporal punishment has adapted to the twenty-first century and is not to be underestimated. 'Formidably conforming' is not idiomatic and conflates adaptation with obedience to a standard.
ghs.remedy: Use 'His corporal punishment has adapted to the twenty-first century, too, so it can't be taken lightly.'

rows.jp: 痕跡を残さず苦痛を与える術に長けているのだ。
rows.en: He knew exactly how to inflict pain without leaving evidence.

ghs.en:
He is excellent in the art of inflicting agony
without leaving any visible trace.

rows.jp: これで某婦人告訴団体ペタも恐くないって寸法さ！
rows.en: That way he had nothing to fear from a certain lawsuit-happy women’s group—let’s call them the PTA!

ghs.en:
And with these measures he has nothing to fear
from that 『Women's Lawsuit Organization * PTA』!

rows.jp: マンモスはそれはもうピグミーマーモセット並に、恐ろしく狡猾な苦しみマッスルなのである。
rows.en: Mammoth was as sly as a pygmy marmoset and built like a mountain of malicious muscle—a walking mass of pain and gain.

ghs.en:
Assuredly, Mammoth has terrifyingly crafty
agony muscles on the level of pygmy marmosets.

rows.jp: 巨体がのしのしと通り過ぎていく。
rows.en: The hulking body stomped past.

ghs.en: His musculature goes lumbering past.

rows.jp: 途中、視線を室内に向けた。
rows.en: Halfway by, he glanced into the room.

ghs.en: Midway, his sight turns inside the room,
ghs.assessment: The person turns his gaze into the room. Making 'sight' itself turn and using 'inside' as its destination is an unidiomatic transfer of the Japanese construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'On the way past, he looked into the room.'

highlights.text: his sight turns inside the room

ghs.en: Shigezo: "..."

rows.jp: そのまま立ち去る。
rows.en: Then he continued on his way.

ghs.en: and with that he leaves.

rows.jp: 原始人に狩られてしまえ、と呪っておく。
rows.en: I put a curse on him: may cavemen hunt him down.

ghs.en: Go get hunted down by a caveman!, I curse him.
ghs.assessment: The curse's content is present, but the English joins a malformed imperative, exclamation point, comma, and reporting clause into an ungrammatical sentence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'May a caveman hunt you down, I cursed him.'

highlights.text: Go get hunted down by a caveman!, I curse him.

rows.jp: 「シベリアの凍土こそ、おまえにふさわしいグレイヴヤードになるだろう」
rows.en: ‘The Siberian permafrost shall be your fitting GRAVEYARD.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "The Siberian tundra would make a fitting graveyard for the likes of you!"

rows.jp: 身を出す。
rows.en: I emerged from hiding.

ghs.en: I show myself.

rows.jp: 「あぶないあぶない」
rows.en: “That was close.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Close so close!"

rows.jp: 「カーテンつけた方がいいですよねぇ、廊下側の窓」
rows.en: “We really ought to put curtains on the windows facing the hall.”

ghs.en: Miyuki: "We should just put up curtains on that corridor window."

rows.jp: 「禁止されてるんだよ。学校もよくわかってるよな」
rows.en: “They’re forbidden. The school knows us too well.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "That was forbidden. School got wise to that already."
ghs.assessment: The source says the curtains are currently prohibited. The past tense implies the prohibition no longer applies and shifts the practical reason they cannot install them.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's forbidden.'

rows.jp: 「いい手がある」
rows.en: “I have an idea.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There's something we could do."
Miyuki: "..."
Tomoki: "..."

rows.jp: 「あー、諸君らが俺をどう思っているかは知っている。だがこれはつまらないギャグではなくマジでいい手なのだ」
rows.en: “I know what you two think of me. But this isn’t one of my stupid jokes. I really do have a good idea.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I know what you ladies think of me. But this isn't some annoying gag, I really think there's something we could do."
ghs.assessment: The collective address means 'you people' or 'all of you' and includes the group present. The English changes it to a gendered address unsupported by the wording and local participants.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I know what you all think of me.'

rows.jp: 「どんなんです？」
rows.en: “What kind of idea?”

ghs.en: Miyuki: "What would that be?"

rows.jp: 「友貴、マシン使えるようにしてくれよ。あとデジカメ」
rows.en: “Tomoki, get the machine running. And grab the digital camera.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Tomoki, get me the machine back in working order. Also, the digital camera."

rows.jp: 「はーん？」
rows.en: “Huh?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Huuuh?"
